primary.thesis: The high strikes ($120 and above) and low strikes ($45 and below) sit at the far tails, which suggests silver was trading somewhere in the $65-$100 range. That fits my recollection that the late-2025/January-2026 parabolic run, and the sharp blow-off and liquidation that followed, reset positioning. CME margin hikes, exchange-driven deleveraging and weaker speculative froth make it hard to rebuild a squeeze big enough for the front-month settlement to reach $120+ within about three months. The rule counts only official settlements, not intraday spikes, which lowers the chance of a touch even more. On the downside, a return below $45 would mean giving back most of the multi-year repricing. The structural support behind that repricing includes solar and industrial deficits, central-bank and retail precious-metals demand, and a weaker dollar backdrop. So the most likely path is a volatile but range-bound front month that touches neither far tail by end of June.

basket.reason: $120 is well above the likely range. After the blow-off and margin hikes, a settlement-basis retest of the prior extremes within one quarter would need a fresh squeeze.
$150 needs a move well beyond the prior cycle highs on a settlement basis. The deeper out-of-the-money strike gives a cushion if silver rallies part of the way.
$45 would mean roughly halving from where silver likely trades and wiping out the 2025-26 repricing. Physical tightness and investment demand make that unlikely by June.
$35 is an extreme downside tail that would need a full collapse of the precious-metals bid. It anchors the range view.

failure_narrative: The basket loses mainly on the upside. A renewed monetary-debasement panic could do it: a dovish or politicised Fed leadership transition, an aggressive rate-cut path, a dollar slide or a fiscal/credit scare, together with physical squeezes (thin COMEX/LBMA inventories, Chinese export restrictions, shortages in Shanghai or India) and heavy retail or ETF inflows. That mix could send the front-month SI settlement back through $120 by June, since silver's high beta to gold amplifies such a move. A smaller risk is a disorderly liquidation cascade. Hawkish Fed repricing, a strong dollar, a cross-asset margin-call deleveraging and exchange margin hikes could together drive settlements under $45.
hedge_thesis: The main way the primary fails is a monetary-debasement or dollar-credibility shock, and that shock would show up just as strongly outside the silver market. Gold would make new highs at or above its extreme strike levels, the dollar index would fall sharply, and markets would price faster or deeper Federal Reserve cuts (or doubt Fed independence under new leadership). Why this works: silver is a leveraged play on gold and on real rates. A move to $120+ in silver is very hard to get unless gold is exploding upward and real yields and the dollar are falling. So contracts on gold hitting high thresholds, on the dollar weakening, or on large or early Fed cuts would pay in the same worlds where the silver NO basket loses.
